label: sound
instruction_covers: VersionSpecifier.compare orders numeric major, minor, patch first, then a release above a prerelease, numeric prerelease identifiers numerically, non-numeric lexically, numeric before non-numeric, and a shorter otherwise-equal identifier list first, with build metadata never affecting precedence
the asserted chain 1.0.0-alpha < alpha.1 < alpha.beta < beta < beta.2 < beta.11 < rc.1 < 1.0.0 is exactly those stated rules
versions_compatible rejects an exact prerelease against its stable release, excludes candidates on the wrong side of a prerelease bound, and treats differing build metadata as compatible
find_possible_versions discards candidates outside the range and returns the remaining original version strings in descending precedence
resolve_to_specific_version returns the highest compatible candidate's original spelling, including build metadata
reduce_versions and the compare return convention are existing public functions whose signatures the instruction says must stay intact
notes: Every asserted case is a direct instance of the Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 precedence rules the instruction enumerates. The runner also reruns the pre-existing test/unit/test_semver.py, which guards the ordinary stable, unbounded-end behavior the instruction says to preserve.
